title: 2026-27 NHL Card Tier List: The Most Popular Hockey Cards on Courtyard
summary: Who are collectors keeping, flipping, or shipping? Explore our 2026-27 NHL card tier list based on real Courtyard pack pulls, from Crosby to Celebrini.
body_markdown:
[The 2026-27 NHL season](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=hockey) is off and running—and everyone has a take.


Can[San Jose’s 20-year-old captain](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/blog-post-macklin-celebrini-rookie-cards-guide) carry the Sharks? What in the world happened in Winnipeg? Will Chicago start playing defense?


As the standings start to take shape, we figured we’d get in on the fun. Instead of putting together a list of the players we believe are the best (and worst) in the National Hockey League, we turned to you, the collectors, to inform our decision on the best hockey cards to collect.


It’s time to play keep, flip, or ship.


On[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) , every collector that purchases[a pack of graded and authenticated digital hockey cards](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=hockey) has a decision to make:[Do they accept the instant buyback offer](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/is-courtyard-io-legit-heres-what-you-need-to-know) for the card they’ve just pulled, keep it in their Courtyard collection, either selling it on[the Courtyard Marketplace](https://courtyard.io/marketplace) (which has zero seller fees) at a later date, or have it[redeemed and shipped to them](https://docs.courtyard.io/courtyard/logistics-and-legal/asset-redemption-and-shipping) so they can proudly display it IRL? Decisions, decisions.


That got us thinking: *Which players do*[hockey card collectors](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=hockey) *on*[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) *choose to keep the most? And does anyone actually want to hold onto a goalie card?*


From legends like[Sidney Crosby](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Sidney%20Crosby&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) and[Alex Ovechkin](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Alex%20Ovechkin&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , to next generation superstars like[Connor McDavid](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Connor%20McDavid&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and onto rising stars like[Macklin Celebrini](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Macklin%20Celebrini&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Connor Bedard](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Connor%20Bedard&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and[Matthew Schaefer](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Matthew%20Schaefer&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , our list isn’t a skills-based ranking judged by on-ice performance; neither McDavid’s ability to turn a defender inside out nor[Connor Hellebuyck](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Connor%20Hellebuyck&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ’s 41-save masterpiece in the Olympic gold medal game has any impact on these rankings. Instead, it’s about how *you* , the collectors on Courtyard, react to the players you pull.


The list below covers dozens of the league’s biggest names, with data based on hockey and sports pack pulls on[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) between August 5th, 2026 and November 3rd, 2026. The big takeaway? Collectors hold onto faces of franchises, young *and* old, while goalies and second-tier stars get flipped.


Tier Category / Sentiment Featured Players


S-Tier The Untouchables (Highest Keep Rates) Auston Matthews, Macklin Celebrini, Quinn Hughes


A-Tier Legends & Rising Stars Sidney Crosby, Cole Caufield, Alex Ovechkin, Jack Hughes, Cutter Gauthier, Lane Hutson, Leo Carlsson


B-Tier Heavily Pulled Superstars & Young Cores Brad Marchand, Kirill Kaprizov, Tim Stutzle, Lucas Raymond, Matvei Michkov, Cale Makar, Jeremy Swayman, Connor McDavid, Connor Bedard, Matthew Schaefer


C-Tier High-Variance & Volume Traded Brock Faber, Charlie McAvoy, Matt Boldy, Tage Thompson, Brandon Hagel, Adam Fox, Moritz Seider, Evgeni Malkin, Wyatt Johnston, Zach Werenski


D-Tier Goalies & Liquidation Targets Connor Hellebuyck, Morgan Geekie, Leon Draisaitl, Spencer Knight, Ilya Sorokin, Drew Doughty, Clayton Keller


F-Tier Instant Flips Artemi Panarin


Without further ado, here are *your* rankings. Time to drop the gloves!


## **S-Tier: Auston Matthews, Macklin Celebrini & Quinn Hughes Have the Most-Kept Hockey Cards on**[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/)


The S-Tier is exclusive; it’s got just three players at the top breathing rarified air—and all three are the kind of players a franchise gets built around:[Auston Matthews](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Auston%20Matthews&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Macklin Celebrini](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Macklin%20Celebrini&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and[Quinn Hughes](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Quinn%20Hughes&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) .


Matthews and Celebrini are two of the most-kept and most-shipped-home players on[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) , which tells you plenty about what hockey collectors on Courtyard are holding: faces of franchises. Matthews is not only the Toronto Maple Leafs’ captain, he also wears the “C” for Team USA, which took home their first Olympic gold since 1980 last winter. Celebrini, meanwhile, is the league’s brightest young star, and is fresh off of a franchise-record 115-point sophomore season. Perhaps that’s why he’s the only player on this list to land among the most-kept, most-shipped, and most-pulled. Collectors keep pulling him—and they’re not giving him back. Demand for the Sharks’ captain is real!


Quinn Hughes, however, is the outlier here. The Norris Trophy-winning defenseman has been a Minnesota Wild blueliner since a blockbuster trade with the Vancouver Canucks in 2025. Yes, he’s a bonafide star, but he also lands above[Sidney Crosby](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Connor%20McDavid&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) and *two* tiers above[Connor McDavid](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Connor%20McDavid&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) —who is also a tier below Quinn’s brother[Jack Hughes](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Jack%20Hughes&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) —two of the sport’s biggest names. Matthews and Celebrini we get, but Hughes certainly stands out.


Collectors have been pulling cards like the 2024 Upper Deck NHL Star Rookies Box Set #13 Macklin Celebrini (PSA 9 MINT) and the 2024 Upper Deck Young Guns Renewed #201 Auston Matthews (PSA 9 Mint) out of[Courtyard.io’s Hockey Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=hockey) more than any other cards of those two players.


## **A-Tier: Alex Ovechkin, Sidney Crosby & Olympic Hero Jack Hughes Just Miss the Top Spot**


Not only are Ovi and Jack Hughes two of the most-pulled players on[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) (we spoil you), they’re also two of the most-kept. That’s a rare combination, and a sign that collectors believe in the future Hall of Famer and league star enough not to take their buyback offers.


With[Ovechkin set to retire at the end of the season](https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/50109700/s-fly-capitals-alex-ovechkin-retire-end-season) , it’s no surprise that hockey card collectors are clamoring for the Russian Machine, who holds the title as the league’s all-time leading goal scorer. Hughes, meanwhile, is the guy who ended a 46-year wait for Team USA, scoring the Golden Goal in overtime against Team Canada to win the Olympic gold. His most-pulled card on Courtyard? A 2026 Topps Now Olympics card, naturally.


The rest of the A-Tier is a nice blend of old guard and new blood.[Sidney Crosby](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Lane%20Hutson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , in his 21st season, is one of the most shipped-home players on the platform, as is the Montreal Canadiens defensemen[Lane Hutson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Lane%20Hutson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , the 2025 Calder Trophy winner, and Anaheim Ducks center[Leo Carlsson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Leo%20Carlsson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) . Hutson’s running mate,[Cole Caufield](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Cole%20Caufield&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , makes it two Canadiens in the A-Tier, and Carlsson’s teammate,[Cutter Gauthier](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Cutter%20Gauthier&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , does the same for the Ducks. Collectors clearly believe in both young cores.


Want a piece of the A-Tier?[Courtyard.io’s Hockey Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=hockey) are where collectors have been pulling cards like the 2005 In The Game Heroes & Prospects #105 Sidney Crosby (PSA 10 GEM MINT) and the 2005 Upper Deck Rookie Class #2 Alexander Ovechkin (PSA 9 MINT), the most-pulled cards for each player.


## **B-Tier: Connor McDavid, Connor Bedard & Matthew Schaefer See Plenty of Pulls, but Less Keeps**


The B-Tier is where things start getting interesting.


[Connor McDavid](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Connor%20McDavid&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Connor Bedard](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Connor%20Bedard&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Matthew Schaefer](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Matthew%20Schaefer&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Kirill Kaprizov](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kirill%20Kaprizov&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and[Matvei Michkov](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Matvei%20Michkov&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) all see plenty of pulls, but none of them land in the A-Tier. Are collectors not sold on Bedard’s potential? Maybe McDavid’s greatness year after year is causing some fatigue. One thing does stand out: No one on this list is over 30.


The rest of the B-Tier is a nice mix of stars and star-adjacent. Players like[Brad Marchand](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Brad%20Marchand&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) and[Lucas Raymond](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Lucas%20Raymond&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) are among the most-kept players on Courtyard, although Raymond’s rough start to the 2026-27 season might have Red Wings fans changing their tune over the coming months.[Cale Makar](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Cale%20Makar&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , a bonafide superstar, is also among the most-shipped-home, while Boston Bruins netminder[Jeremy Swayman](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Jeremy%20Swayman&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) marks the first goalie on the list.


Are you riding with the Blackhawks or Islanders this season?[Courtyard.io’s Hockey Master Pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/hockey-master-pack) has a 2023 Upper Deck Premier Acetate Rookie Autograph Patch #ARCB Connor Bedard rookie card (PSA 9 MINT) and a 2025 Upper Deck #451 Matthew Schaefer - Outburst rookie card (PSA 9 MINT) waiting to be pulled.


## **C-Tier: Matt Boldy, Zach Werenski & the Olympic Heroes Getting Flipped**


If there’s one thing the data makes clear, it’s that Team USA’s gold medal could only buy so much collector loyalty.


[Matt Boldy](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Matt%20Boldy&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) scored[the opening goal in the gold medal game](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ezhEZB0ku78) , a goal some considered the best of the entire competition, and[Zach Werenski](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Zach%20Werenski&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) made the pass that set up Jack Hughes’ overtime winner. Both are among the most-flipped hockey players on[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) , with Brandon Hagel of the Tampa Bay Lightning keeping them company. Werenski gave Hughes the Golden Goal, and collectors gave him the buyback button. Tough crowd.


Not everyone in the C-Tier is getting cashed out quickly, though.[Tage Thompson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Tage%20Thompson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) and[Adam Fox](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Adam%20Fox&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) are both among the most-kept players on the platform.


Think collectors are sleeping on Boldy?[Courtyard.io’s Hockey Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=hockey) are where collectors have been pulling the 2022 Upper Deck #201 Matt Boldy (PSA 8 NM-MT).


## **D-Tier: Connor Hellebuyck, Leon Draisaitl & the Goalies Getting the Buyback Treatment**


The D-Tier is where we start to see goalies take center ice.


Start with[Connor Hellebuyck](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Connor%20Hellebuyck&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) . The former Hart and Vezina Trophy Winner made 41 saves in the Olympic gold medal game, then had an offseason that went about as poorly as it could, from a public trade request and a suspension to a trade to the New Jersey Devils in October. It’s tough to tell if hockey card collectors are souring on him because of the drama or simply not as interested in goalies in general, but the fact that such a decorated player is landing all the way down on this list tells you something.


Fellow netminder[Ilya Sorokin](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Ilya%20Sorokin&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) of the New York Islanders, one of the league’s best goalies, also makes the D-Tier, alongside[Spencer Knight](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Spencer%20Knight&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) of the Chicago Blackhawks, who has had a rough start to the season to say the least.


Then there’s[Leon Draisaitl](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Leon%20Draisaitl&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) . He finished second to Hellebuyck in the 2025 Hart Trophy voting, and helps power the Oilers’ incredible offense, yet sits near the bottom of the list. Maybe collectors are just too focused on his teammate Connor McDavid.


Think the buyback crowd has this one wrong? We’ve been eyeing the 2014 Upper Deck #223 Leon Draisaitl rookie card (PSA 10 GEM MINT), which is valued at $786, waiting to be pulled from[Courtyard.io’s Hockey Pro Pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/hockey-pro-pack) .


## **F-Tier: Artemi Panarin, the Lone Instant Flip**


The F-Tier is the end of the line, and this year it’s a party of one:[Artemi Panarin](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Artemi%20Panarin&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) of the Los Angeles Kings.


Here’s the thing about “The Breadman”: He was the New York Rangers’ leading scorer every season he spent with the club, following a brief stint in Columbus and three 70+-point seasons for the Chicago Blackhawks. Sure, he’s 35, but he’s got another year left on his contract with the Kings. Does Panarin really deserve this? We’re talking about a perennial point-per-game scorer who plays in a big market, here!


If you think Panarin is undervalued, his 2015 Upper Deck #221 rookie card (PSA 9 Mint) is waiting for you in[Courtyard.io’s Hockey Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=hockey) .


## **How to Get Graded Hockey Cards on**[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) ****


From superstars like Auston Matthews on down to aging scorers like Artemi Panarin, our NHL tier list is a little different from the usual hockey rankings that judge players by points-per-game or save percentage. This list is about what *you* , hockey card collectors, decide to do when you pull a player’s cardboard on[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) .


When[buying hockey cards on Courtyard](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=hockey) , you have three choices: keep, flip, or ship.
